sections.description:
These items are rolled before other drops and replace any other drops if successful.

First, if the player is on an appropriate slayer task, there is a 1/3052 (1/3021 with tier 3 or higher luck) chance to recieve a wand or orb (so 1/6104 each). If not successful or not on-task, there is a 1/1024 (1/993 with tier 3 luck) chance to recieve a whip.

If both of these rolls fail and a Most Wanted card (abyssal demons) is carried, a second more generous roll for each is performed. If on task, a 1/2900 roll (1/2871 with tier 3 luck) roll for wand/orb, and then a 1/973 roll (1/963 with tier 3 luck) for a whip. Combining all these chances give a 1/2976.0 chance for a wand or orb (each; 1/2946.1 with tier 3 luck) per on-task kill, and a 1/499.4 chance for a whip (1/489.4 with tier 3 luck) per on-task kill (off-task is slightly more likely at 1/499.2 and 1/489.1). If one of these second rolls results in a drop, additional charges are consumed from the card: 4 for a whip, 19 for an orb, and 99 for a wand, in addition to the normal 1 charge per kill.

drops.name: Sakirth's journal
drops.notes:
Journals are dropped in order and only after the completion of Hero's Welcome in Dragonkin Lair: Sakirth's, Strisath's, Kalibath's, Phalaks'. Each journal has a threshold of kills (100, 300, 500 and 700, respectively) and every kill after this threshold decreases the denominator by 1 until the drop is guaranteed. Sakirth's journal is guaranteed after a kill count of 199, Strisath's at 399, Kalibath's at 599, and Phalaks' at 799.

Having the Lorehound pet summoned with the Lore Helper perk decreases the denominator by 20.

sections.description:
When Araxxi is killed, her corpse remains and acts as a reward coffer to collect the drops. Having tier 4 luck increases the chances of obtaining unique rewards from Araxxi's corpse. The ring may be put on after killing but prior to looting.

The drop table will always roll on three tables; 100%, food/potions and main table drop once. Effigies from Araxxi are considered a primary drop. A roll will also be made on pets (the araxyte pet itself and then eggs if eligible), leg pieces and "Add-on" drops. These three drops are all tertiary drops, so it is possible to obtain all three from one kill, although exceedingly rare.

Araxxi's corpse offers the same mechanics as the Queen Black Dragon's reward chest, where rewards may be collected into the inventory, sent straight to the bank, or be abandoned. Players without an araxyte pet also have the option of sacrificing all of their drops for a second chance at the pet. Gambling your rewards will double the drop rate of the pet, effectively tripling the original drop rate. This feature is removed once the player obtains the pet, either normally or through gambling.

The current rage level only affects the drop rate of the araxyte pheromone and the araxyte pet.

Araxxi does not have access to the rare drop table.

Araxxi's body will always contain araxyte arrows, unless an araxyte pheromone or a crystal triskelion fragment is obtained, which replace them. Starved ancient effigy can be rewarded with araxyte arrows.

sections.description:
In hard mode, the rewards are obtained through a streak/enrage system. After each kill, players have the option to continue the challenge, or claim the rewards. One reward is given at a time, but the quantity of these items increases with higher killstreak and possibly enrage. Likewise, if the player dies during their streak, part of their accumulated rewards is lost based on the amount of killstreak the player had prior to their death. This starts at 5% saved for 1 killstreak and caps at 75% saved at 15+ killstreak, rounded down. This reduction applies by whole numbers of the items held in the chest, not the total value of rewards. If the Arch-Glacor is defeated but a lingering attack subsequently kills the player, they will be sent to Death's office but the killstreak will not be terminated. With the exception of the glacor core and Chaos die reroll tokens, no charms or other secondary drops are obtainable in hard mode.

It was worked out by the players that the equation for the unique item drop rates could be:

Where e is the enrage of Arch-Glacor and s is the number of total kills done in the streak (so Streak+1 if using the Streak value in the loot interface).

This is more easily interpreted as:

Where it can be seen that the base chance is 1/666, and increases by 1/666 for every 100 enrage or 60 kills in streak.

The validity of these formulae remains unconfirmed, but it matches the known drop rates at different streaks and enrages given from the reveal of the drop rates from the Elder God Wars Dungeon.

When the unique item table is rolled, the player has the chance for the following:

The quantity of items added after each kill seems to follow the formula Quantity=⌊Base Quantity×(1+0.1×Streak)⌋+Luck bonus

When claiming streaks, if the player's inventory and bank is full, any remaining rewards will remain inside the chest. If the player logs out before claiming these drops, they will be lost. They will be withdrawn in noted form if this occurs.

Common items dropped in hard mode have a fixed rarity and a variable quantity; there is a base quantity which is then scaled by the enrage and streak length. Unique items have a fixed quantity of 1 but a variable drop rate; the drop chance is affected by enrage and streak length.

sections.description:
Automaton generators encountered during The World Wakes drop nothing.

The initial roll for uniques is 1/512 (1/506 with tier 3 or higher luck active), followed by a 1/2 roll to get tracking gloves or cresbot - if cresbot is already owned or unlocked, 45,000-55,000 coins are dropped instead. If a Most Wanted card (automatons) is carried, a second more generous roll is performed: 1/486 (1/481 with tier 3 luck). If the second roll succeeds, cresbot is guaranteed to be dropped if not yet unlocked, and tracking gloves are guaranteed if it is (there is no coins option for the second roll). Combining all these chances gives a roughly 1/330 chance per kill for gloves once cresbot is unlocked (1/326.5 with tier 3 luck). If the second roll results in a unique drop, 99 charges are drained from the card, in addition to the usual 1 charge per kill.

Receiving a unique prevents all other drops except charms.

sections.description:
Automaton guardians encountered during The World Wakes drop nothing.

The initial roll for uniques is 1/512 (1/506 with tier 3 or higher luck active), followed by a 1/2 roll to get static gloves or cresbot - if cresbot is already owned or unlocked, 45,000-55,000 coins are dropped instead. If a Most Wanted card (automatons) is carried, a second more generous roll is performed: 1/486 (1/481 with tier 3 luck). If the second roll succeeds, cresbot is guaranteed to be dropped if not yet unlocked, and static gloves are guaranteed if it is (there is no coins option for the second roll). Combining all these chances gives a roughly 1/330 chance per kill for gloves once cresbot is unlocked (1/326.5 with tier 3 luck). If the second roll results in a unique drop, 99 charges are drained from the card, in addition to the usual 1 charge per kill.

Receiving a unique prevents all other drops except charms.

sections.description:
The main drop table is split into two versions.

The first version is tied to the barbarians that have Acelin, Adelino, Adolpho, Edelschwarz, Fafner, Gutrune, Hagen, Lydspor, Siegfried, Sieglinde, or Wotan as their name in their examine text. sections.title: Cards

sections.description: When Beastmaster Durzag is killed, his corpse remains and acts as a reward coffer to collect the drops. Durzag has several drop tables that are rolled on to constitute the loot. Airut bones are always received, the consumable table is always rolled, summoning charms are commonly received, and tertiary drops may be received. If the unique drops table rolls either a Mazcab ability codex or piece of achto equipment, the main drop will not be received. If the unique drops table rolls teci, the main drop table will be rolled multiple times.
sections.title: Rewards / 100%

sections.description:
Beastmaster Durzag can only drop one item from this table. If no armour piece or Mazcab ability codex is dropped, the player will receive teci.

Armour is gained from Beastmaster Durzag in the following order: boots, gloves, then helmet.

Progressing in the drop order requires collecting all three of the previous equipment slot's achto equipment - so in order to receive an Achto Primeval helmet, they would have to get all Achto Tempest, Primeval, and Teralith boots and gloves. The Achto equipment gained from each equipment slot is based on the combat style the player dealt the most damage with during the kill they obtained that armour; if the equipment piece corresponding to the used style is not owned, that is always gotten before the others, and otherwise there are equal odds of obtaining armour corresponding to one of the unused styles.

A player that owns all nine pieces of achto boots, gloves, and helmets may continue to receive achto armour as drops, but the drop order will no longer be enforced. For example, it is possible to receive a second Achto Teralith Helm, followed by a second Achto Teralith gloves.

When killed in the wilderness with achto armour, it will drop a specified amount of coins if you die.

Otherwise, the chosen armour piece is determined by the missing armour pieces (in order: boots, gloves, helmet, legs and body) and the combat style used.

drops.name: Inert black stone crystal
drops.notes:
Inert black stone crystal has a base drop rate of 1/300 in solo, 1/1,000 in duo, and 1/1,500 in trio, with thresholds of 60, 200, and 300, respectively. Example: If a player were to have 101 group and 144 solo (combined 245), it would be 4 thresholds for solo, 1 threshold for duo, and 0 thresholds for trio.

Rolled for before the rest of the main drop table and replaces that drop if obtained.

Jagex. Mod Orion's Twitter account. 10 October 2018. (Archived from the original on 30 May 2020.) Mod Orion: "Futon has 245 kills: You have a 4x higher chance to receive the pet on solo mode. You have not yet reached the threshold on group mode."

Jagex. Mod Orion's Twitter account. 10 October 2018. (Archived from the original on 30 May 2020.) Mod Orion: "Correct. We're VERY happy that our systems allow us to re-use the previous elite dungeon code for new ones."

Jagex. Mod Orion's Twitter account. 17 May 2019. (Archived from the original on 17 May 2019.) Mod Orion: "Elite dungeon duo pet rates and thresholds btw"

Jagex. Mod Sponge's Twitter account. 7 December 2021. (Archived from the original on 16 April 2022.) Mod Sponge: "If you happen to roll pet, you never reach this table (it is a separate roll, that returns before this is reached)"

sections.description:
In order to receive a drop, the player must deal at least 500 damage to the demon boss in a single hit. Once this condition is met, a notification will be given to the player stating that they have dealt a "powerful blow". The player must also stay in combat with the boss until it dies to be eligible for the rewards. If the player leaves or dies, the hit of 500 damage needs to be done again to still get a drop. Players will only be able to do this until the boss reaches 10% of its total health (40,000 life points); any attempts to initiate combat with a demon boss after this threshold will notify the player they are too late to be eligible for a reward from this fight. This doesn't apply for the normal drops given to the player who dealt most damage to the boss.

A demon boss will always drop a minimum of five drops. A single player can receive five separate drops if they manage to defeat it alone. If two to four players defeat a demon, drops will be split amongst the top damage-dealing participants. Each player that receives a drop will also receive infernal ashes.

Demon slayer equipment and title scrolls are dropped alongside any other drops that are received. For example, a player that receives an off-hand demon slayer crossbow will also get any of the other normal drops it gives. Both a piece of demon slayer equipment and a title scroll can drop in one kill - the same player cannot receive both, unless the demon was killed solo. Only one demon slayer item and one title can be dropped per kill.

Fighting a Flash Mob in the Wilderness gives you a greater chance of getting a demon slayer equipment drop, and other drops are slightly more valuable than at other spawn locations.

drops.name: The Magister's Journal #1
drops.notes:
The books are dropped in order; the next book can only be received after reading the previous book. The higher a player's killcount, the higher chance of a book being dropped.

After 450 total kills of corrupted creatures and soul devourers, the denominator begins to decrease by 1 for every further kill until the item is guaranteed to be obtained at 899 kills.

drops.name: The Magister's Journal #2
drops.notes:
The books are dropped in order; the next book can only be received after reading the previous book. The higher a player's killcount, the higher chance of a book being dropped.

After 1,350 total kills of corrupted creatures and soul devourers, the denominator begins to decrease by 1 for every further kill until the item is guaranteed to be obtained at 1,799 kills.

drops.name: The Magister's Journal #3
drops.notes:
The books are dropped in order; the next book can only be received after reading the previous book. The higher a player's killcount, the higher chance of a book being dropped.

After 2,250 total kills of corrupted creatures and soul devourers, the denominator begins to decrease by 1 for every further kill until the item is guaranteed to be obtained at 2,699 kills.

sections.description:
Loot is awarded from the corpse of Flesh-hatcher Mhekarnahz on a separate platform, with "Bank All", "Take All", and "Abandon All" options. Seven rolls on the tables below are awarded for each kill in addition to a guaranteed drop from the charm table. Some items may be rolled repeatedly. A new fight cannot be started without banking, taking, or abandoning rewards from the previous kill.

Flesh-hatcher Mhekarnahz does not appear to have access to the rare drop table.

sections.description:
After fighting the mole, it is decided if a rare unique item will be dropped, and what that item is, before attributing it to a player. The odds of any rare item dropping at all are 1/10. After it is determined that a rare item will drop, which specific item is to be dropped is determined using a 52-slot table. This rare item is then distributed to one of the top three players, or to the single player if fighting the mole solo. All of the mole's special drops (clingy moles, numbing roots, dragon 2h swords, and ultra-growth potions) are tertiary drops. Whenever someone receives a special drop from the mole, it will be announced in the message box.

The drop mechanics for the mole function differently in a group than when fought solo. Namely, the player to deal the most damage will always receive big bones and a mole claw if on a members' world, or only big bones if on a F2P world; the three players to deal the most damage will receive three mole skins, distributed equally (if the group is two players, there is a random chance for either player to receive two, and the other will receive one), all players who have completed the elite Falador achievement set will receive a mole nose, and players doing the Fur 'n Seek wishlist will sometimes receive long, sharp claws. The regular item drops are then divided equally between the top 3 players; if the drop quantity does not divide equally, the remainder is given to a random player of the top three that did not receive a rare drop.

In hard mode, rare unique drops are more common, while some items are dropped in larger quantities.

Following the 27 January 2014 update, the giant mole no longer has access to the rare drop table.

drops.name: Big bones
drops.notes: In a group, the big bones and mole claw are received by the player that dealt the most damage.

drops.name: Mole claw (m)
drops.notes: In a group, the big bones and mole claw are received by the player that dealt the most damage.

drops.name: Mole skin
drops.notes: In a group, the mole skins are distributed amongst the three players that dealt the most damage.

drops.name: Mole nose (m)
drops.notes:

sections.description:
The player has a 1/128 (1/126 with tier 3 or higher luck active) chance of accessing this table. Every drop on this table then has equal chance of being accessed, making every individual drop 1/1,280 (1/1260 with tier 3 luck). In addition to the 7 specific drops displayed on the table below, the player also has a chance at receiving 1 random tree seed, 4 random noted herbs, or 2 random noted herbs, for a total of 10 possible drops.

If the player is carrying a Most Wanted card (glacors) and they fail to access this table, a second roll is performed to attempt to drop boots. This roll is a more generous 1/406 (1/401 with tier 3 luck), which then drops one of the three boots (1/3 chance each). Combining these chances gives an overall 1/626.6 chance to receive each type of boot per kill (1/617.9 with tier 3 luck). Receiving boots as a result of the second roll will drain 99 charges from the card, in addition to the 1 charge per kill. It is worth noting that the second roll is not performed if something else from this table is dropped, as the check is only for accessing this table.

sections.description:
These raiders will shout various phrases, and each time they shout this, one roll for a raided drop (logs for a wood-gathering goblin, seeds for a goblin on a farm, stone spirits for a mine) is added to that goblin. When it is killed, they drop all of it. For example, if a goblin raider is cutting trees and yells three quotes, then the player has three rolls on the raided logs drop table. These are dropped in addition to a main drop and any other tertiary drops.

The quality of resource is not limited to the source they are targeting. A Raider gathering at a normal tree can drop yew logs, for example.

sections.description: Each kill of a sinkholes monster has a chance to drop a card. If a card has not yet been dropped for the player the chance is 1/3, else if the monster is combat level 85 or higher the chance is 1/4, otherwise the chance is 1/6. If a card is dropped, one of them is dropped from the distribution: 16% for each of locust, leech, and mantis; 10% for each of mosquito, yak, and bunyip; 8% for titan; 5% for meerkats; and 3% for each of ibis, phoenix, and smoke devil.

sections.description:
Guthan's crypt is located at the south-east of the Barrows area, and he is weak to Air Spells. Strong magic spells such as Air Surge, Polypore Strike and Smoke Barrage are recommended when fighting him, however he can be taken down just as easily with strong melee weapons such as the Chaotic Maul. Guthan does not pose as much of a threat as his brothers do, with his set effect healing him instead of dealing extra damage or draining stats/adrenaline, but players should still be cautious and well-prepared when fighting him.

Guthan does not drop his main rewards directly; instead, his equipment is added as possible rewards from the Barrows chest. See The Barrows Brothers#Rewards for more information. However, Guthan can directly drop the following items.

sections.description: Each kill of a sinkholes monster has a chance to drop a card. If a card has not yet been dropped for the player the chance is 1/3, else if the monster is combat level 85 or higher the chance is 1/4, otherwise the chance is 1/6. If a card is dropped, one of them is dropped from the distribution: 16% for each of locust, leech, and mantis; 10% for each of mosquito, yak, and bunyip; 8% for titan; 5% for meerkats; and 3% for each of ibis, phoenix, and smoke devil.

sections.title: Weapons

sections.description: Regardless of chest auto-loot settings, all tertiary drops except vital sparks and soul talismans are dropped to the ground.

drops.name: Soul talisman
drops.notes: Jagex. Mod Orion's Twitter account. 16 February 2019. (Archived from the original on 17 February 2019.) Mod Orion: "Nope, they're 1/200 from sarcophagi and from killing akhs."

drops.name: Vital spark
drops.notes: 1 base; +1 for being on a Slayer assignment; +1 if a vital spark drop enhancer is held.

drops.name: Key to the Crossing
drops.notes: Increased to 1/75 while on a Slayer assignment. Increased to 1/395 (1/60 on-task) when carrying a Sophanem slayer dungeon drop enhancer.

drops.name: Khopesh of the Kharidian
drops.notes: Increased to 1/8,000 when on Slayer assignment.

drops.name: Corrupted gem
drops.notes: Can only be dropped during a Slayer task.

drops.name: The Magister's Journal #1
drops.notes:
The books are dropped in order; the next book can only be received after reading the previous book. The higher a player's killcount, the higher chance of a book being dropped.

After 200 total kills of corrupted creatures and soul devourers, the denominator begins to decrease by 1 for every further kill until the item is guaranteed to be obtained at 399 kills.

drops.name: The Magister's Journal #2
drops.notes:
The books are dropped in order; the next book can only be received after reading the previous book. The higher a player's killcount, the higher chance of a book being dropped.

After 600 total kills of corrupted creatures and soul devourers, the denominator begins to decrease by 1 for every further kill until the item is guaranteed to be obtained at 799 kills.

sections.description:
The Kalphite King's regular drops (excluding unique items) are fairly unique compared to other monsters - rather than dropping one large amount, it drops smaller quantities which are then multiplied accordingly upon being rolled. In free-for-all groups, the whole drop goes to the player who dealt the most damage. In LootShare and CoinShare, the drops are split accordingly based on LootShare potential. For clarity, the whole drop (multipliers included) are listed on the table below rather than individual groups.

sections.description:
Upon defeat, three drop piles are awarded per kill. In solo encounters, the player receives all three drops. In duo encounters, the leftover drop is awarded to the top damaging player. In trio encounters, every player gets their own drop.

Like at Solak, Guardian of the Grove, drops from Kerapac are announced in local chat and separated into three different colours; main drops are green, secondary drops are blue, while rare unique drops are orange.

Up to three stacks are received per kill.

sections.description:
The chance of obtaining a piece of the fractured staff of Armadyl is 1/400 per loot pile, or ~1/133 per solo boss kill. If the player has never had a staff component drop before or has equal numbers of each piece on their drop log, a random component of the three (Staff of Armadyl's fractured shaft, Fractured stabilisation gem, Fractured Armadyl symbol) is dropped; the drop will be the next piece missing in the sequence of shaft, gem, symbol. The drop chance is improved to 1/392 with the enriched pontifex shadow ring active, 1/396 with tier 4 luck active, or 1/388 with both active.

If the staff component roll fails, there is a 1/180 chance of obtaining the scripture, wrist wraps or codex per loot pile (one of the three is chosen at random), or ~1/60 per solo boss kill. The drop chance is improved to 1/176 with the enriched pontifex shadow ring active, 1/178 with tier 4 luck active, or 1/174 with both active.

This, in turn, means a ~1/124 chance for any unique drops per loot pile, or a ~1/41 chance per solo boss kill (~1/120 per pile, ~1/40 per solo kill with the enriched shadow pontifex ring and tier 4 luck active).

Last Riders is dropped to all players (regardless of whether they participate in the kill, or are even in the room). It remains for approximately 30 seconds before disappearing. Has a base drop rate of 1/1,000, but after 1,000 kill count, each kill will decrease the denominator by 1, so it is a guaranteed drop on a solo kill with a kill count of at least 1,999.

Having a Lorehound summoned with the Lore Helper perk increases the drop rate.

They are rolled after uniques, charms, triskelions, rare drop table, and wilderness shared loot table - but before clue scrolls. This effectively gives a 61/70 (~87.1%) chance to roll the rest of the regular drop table (185/224, ~82.6% with tier 3 luck or higher)

If a card has not yet been dropped for the player the chance is 1/3, else if the monster is combat level 85 or higher the chance is 1/4, otherwise the chance is 1/6. sections.description:
The Angel of Death has two tables; the first drop table is the main drop table, where unique items (wand, core, codex, and chest) can be rolled. The main drop table can be accessed by holding Nex's aggression the longest (capped at 1 player) or dealing the most damage (capped at 6 players) - therefore, each kill always has seven rolls on the main drop table, provided that seven players survived the encounter. All rolls are independent of each other, so it's possible to get multiple unique drops per kill, albeit very rare.

A second, inferior drop table is awarded to the next top three damage dealers who are not eligible to roll for the main drop table. This is only accessible when fighting Nex in a group of eight or larger, and does not have access to the unique items.

Regardless, both drop tables have access to the blood tentacle pet unlock item.

The chance per person to obtain either the wand of the praesul or the imperium core is 1/(142×n) where n is the player count at the beginning of the fight; this is done such that the expected number of wands/cores come out to the same number per kill: 1/142 (given the player count is between 1 and 7). The per person drop rate to receive either a wand or core for team sizes of 8 or higher is 1/5000 for those who roll on the primary table. After the changes released on 7 May 2019, the praesul codex has a drop rate of 1/(36×min(7,n)) per person; this is done such that the expected number of codices come out to the same number per kill: 1/36 (after failing to receive either the wand or core). Therefore, the expected number of wand, core or codex drops per kill is approximately 1/29.

Unlike the base Nex encounter, the Angel of Death does not have access to the rare drop table.

sections.description:
When the Phoenix is mortally wounded, she will move to the pyre. The player must then set the pyre on fire, burning the Phoenix and turning her to ash. She will quickly be reborn. The player may then speak with the new Phoenix and be rewarded with two phoenix quills.

For every kill, the player will also receive 250 Slayer experience (5,000 Slayer experience is awarded the first time she is killed), 3,750 Firemaking experience, 1,500 Fletching experience, and 500 Crafting experience as a reward for defeating her, as well as a 1/100 chance to get a phoenix eggling pet. In order to roll for the pet, the player has to exit via the cave entrance instead of teleporting out.

sections.title: Main

sections.description:
After restoring the enchantment and returning the Queen to her slumber, the player may enter a rewards room with a dragonkin coffer containing their spoils. The coffer rolls on three different drop tables at once; the 100% drops, a main drop, and consumables. Unique drops, if rolled, are added on the side as tertiary rewards.

Rewards can be withdrawn either in noted or unnoted form, the default is unnoted. There are options to "Bank all", "Take all", and "Abandon all", along with right-click for all three options on each item. If the noted option is not selected, the "Take all" button results in the player's inventory being full of all of the unnoted items of that variant. The "Abandon all" option can also be used, which discards all of the items from the coffer. Items stay in the coffer until the player logs out or leaves the chamber. Having tier 3 or higher luck will increase the chance of unique items from the chest.

If the player clicks on the coffer but does not claim the rewards, and later logs out or loses connection, the rewards will be sent to the player's bank.

Collecting all four dragonkin journals is a requirement to trim the completionist cape and to obtain the master quest cape.

sections.description:
Raksha does not drop items upon defeat; rather, the Keeper will place an item in front of the security projector in the antechamber to be picked up. In duo encounters, each player receives their own reward. The drop rates between solo and duo mode are the same. If no drop appears, it is due to an active drop cleaner, such as seedicide or spring cleaner 9001.

There is a 1/50 chance of rolling the unique table, or 1/49 with tier 4 luck active. If this table is rolled, the item will appear alongside the main drop.

On average, a Raksha kill will give 1,880,201 coins in rare drops only.

sections.description: There are two rolls made on this table simultaneously; one for the weapons and another for the robes. Therefore, it is possible, although rare, to get two unique pieces of First Necromancer's equipment from one kill. The chance to hit the weapon table is 1/320, improved to 1/316 with tier 4 luck. The chance to hit the armour table is 1/128, improved to 1/126 with tier 4 luck. Therefore, the chance to hit either the weapon or armour table is ~1/92, improved to ~1/91 with tier 4 luck. sections.description:
Revenant drops are not affected by luck. There are only two ways to increase the drop rate of revenant items: completion of the elite Wilderness achievements which gives a 5% increased chance for revenant drops, and revenant drop enhancers, which give a 10% increased chance. Both boosts can be in effect at the same time.

The ghostlevel used to calculate the drop rates of the revenant cyclops's unique items is 7, and the revnumber is 8571. Drop chances are increased by 5% if elite Wilderness achievements are completed, and by 10% if the revenant drop enhancer in the backpack or currency pouch, stacks with the former.

drops.name: Coins
drops.notes:
The maximum amount of coins that can be received is equal to fifty times the ghostlevel (7), and the minimum is always 50.

If on a relevant Slayer task, coins chance slightly reduced and replaced by ancient warriors equipment patch.

Coins are a guaranteed drop if no unique drop is received.

drops.notes: Only while on a relevant Slayer task. This is a separate roll to the Wilderness shared loot table which does not require on-task.

sections.description: Before the update on 25 February 2009, river trolls were a random event that occurred while a player was fishing. These NPC monsters would appear and attack players when the player initially made an attempt to fish. They would say "Fishes be mine!" before attacking the player. The river troll's combat level used to vary depending on that of the player's, up to a maximum of level 159. Like most other random events at the time, the river troll could be fled from, as it only had a melee attack.

drops.notes:
Chipped black stone crystal has a base drop rate of 1/300 with a threshold of 60. Example: If a player were to have 101 group and 144 solo (combined 245), it would be 4 thresholds for solo, 1 threshold for duo and 0 thresholds for trio.

Rolled for before the rest of the main drop table and replaces that drop if obtained.

sections.description: Each kill of a sinkholes monster has a chance to drop a card. If a card has not yet been dropped for the player the chance is 1/3, else if the monster is combat level 85 or higher the chance is 1/4, otherwise the chance is 1/6. If a card is dropped, one of them is dropped from the distribution: 16% for each of locust, leech, and mantis; 10% for each of mosquito, yak, and bunyip; 8% for titan; 5% for meerkats; and 3% for each of ibis, phoenix, and smoke devil.

sections.title: Other

sections.description:
Talking to Solak or Merethiel will award loot inside the instance. If this is not claimed or if the player died when the team successfully completed the encounter, they can be claimed from Merethiel outside the arena instead. Killcount is not awarded for the latter. Completing another encounter without claiming rewards will automatically forfeit the previous loot. Drop rates are the same across all team sizes.

Like Nex: Angel of Death, player drops are completely independent of each other, so it's possible to get multiple unique drops from one kill. If the player's inventory is full, then the items are sent to the bank, apart from clue scrolls, which are dropped on the ground. Clue scrolls received from Solak bypass the soft cap on the number of clue scrolls owned.

sections.description: There is a 1/55 chance to roll for any eldritch crossbow piece. A random part will be dropped first, and the next one will be dropped following the sequence: limb, stock and mechanism.

drops.name: Eldritch crossbow limb
drops.notes: Random part dropped first, then the next roll on this table guarantees one of the other two pieces. Duplicated parts act as if they were non-existent, so if a player obtained a doubled stock as their first part, then they would obtain another stock after getting a limb and mechanism drop. Using a Hazelmere's signet ring does not have a chance to double items.

drops.name: Umbral urn
drops.notes:
Has a base drop rate of 1/300 (solo encounters), 1/1000 (duo encounters), or 1/1,500 (trio encounters), with a threshold of 60 for solo encounters, 200 for duo and 300 for trio encounters (combined solo and group killcount). Example: If a player were to have 101 group and 144 solo (combined 245), it would be 4 thresholds for solo, 1 threshold for duo and 0 thresholds for trio.

Jagex. Mod Orion's Twitter account. 10 October 2018. (Archived from the original on 30 May 2020.) Mod Orion: "Futon has 245 kills: You have a 4x higher chance to receive the pet on solo mode. You have not yet reached the threshold on group mode."

Jagex. Mod Orion's Twitter account. 10 October 2018. (Archived from the original on 30 May 2020.) Mod Orion: "Correct. We're VERY happy that our systems allow us to re-use the previous elite dungeon code for new ones."

Jagex. Mod Orion's Twitter account. 17 May 2019. (Archived from the original on 17 May 2019.) Mod Orion: "Elite dungeon duo pet rates and thresholds btw"

drops.notes: The player must have completed the Temple of Aminishi, followed by the Dragonkin Laboratory, and finally the Shadow Reef in consecutive order to receive an elite chest. All three Elite Dungeons must be done in Normal Mode, but it does not matter if they are completed solo or in a group. There is a 1/15 chance of receiving an ultra elite chest instead.

sections.description: The main drop table is rolled out of 256. This is reduced to 253 if tier 3 or higher luck is active, which slightly reduces the chance of a fire talisman drop, and increases the chances of other main drops. Dragon platebody parts are rolled separately.

There is a 1/352 chance to access the dragon platebody part table (1/348 with tier 3 or higher luck active). If successful, one of the three parts is chosen (1/3 chance each).

If a Most Wanted card (tormented demons) is carried, and if none of the uniques are selected (dragon platebody parts, dragon claws, dragon limbs), a second more generous roll is performed for each. For dragon platebody parts this is 1/334 (1/331 with tier 3 luck). Combining these chances gives an overall 1/515.9 chance to get each dragon platebody part per kill (1/509.9 with tier 3 luck). If the second roll results in a drop, additional charges are consumed from the card: 19 for dragon platebody parts.

Receiving a dragon platebody part prevents all other drops except charms.

sections.title: Pre-roll

sections.description:
Dragon claws (both are dropped as one drop) and dragon limbs each have a 1/256 chance to be dropped, as part of the main drop table (1/253 with tier 3 luck).

If a Most Wanted card (tormented demons) is carried, and if none of the uniques are selected (dragon platebody parts, dragon claws, dragon limbs), a second more generous roll is performed for each. For dragon claws and limbs, this is 1/243 (1/240 with tier 3 luck), after the second roll for dragon platebody parts; if successful, one of the two items is selected (1/2 for claws, 1/2 limbs). Combining these chances gives an overall 1/168.6 chance to dragon claws or limbs per kill (1/166.6 with tier 3 luck). If the second roll results in a drop, additional charges are consumed from the card: 19 for dragon claws and 99 for dragon limbs.

Although TzTok-Jad does not drop any items directly, defeating it rewards the player with several items, as they will have successfully completed the TzHaar Fight Cave.

drops.name: Seismic wand
drops.notes:
When Vorago is killed, up to 5 players are eligible to receive loot, but only one person can obtain a rare item.

Vorago's seismic weapons constitute the normal drop in a drop pile. The chance of getting a specific seismic item is 1/400 per item per slot, making any seismic drop 1/200 per slot, or 1/40 per kill; however, only 1 unique weapon can be dropped per kill, if at all. During hard mode, drop chance for any seismic is 1/100 per slot, or 1/20 per kill. Drop rate increased by 1% with tier 4 luck.

1/5,000 per drop pile, or 1/2,500 while in hard mode. If a player who already owns a Vitalis receives this drop, it will be rerolled to a random player who does not. This is the "per drop" chance, where Vorago gives 5 drops per kill. As such, the "per kill" drop chance (the chance that at least one is dropped in Vorago's 5 drops) is between 1/1,001 and 1/1,000 (or between 1/501 and 1/500 in hard mode). If 5 players each obtain one of the drop pile, their individual chances are 1/5,000 (1/2500 in hard mode). This drop has a threshold of 1,000.

Jagex. Mod Chris L's Twitter account. 9 February 2015. (Archived from the original on 24 March 2015.) Mod Chris L: "1/5k per drop, so should be 1/1k kills"

sections.title: Tertiary

sections.description:
When Yakamaru is killed, its helmet remains and acts as a reward coffer to collect the drops. Yakamaru has several drop tables that are rolled on to constitute the loot. The consumable table is always rolled, summoning charms are commonly received, and tertiary drops may be received. If the unique drops table rolls either a Mazcab ability codex or piece of achto equipment, the main drop will not be received. If the unique drops table rolls Teci, the main drop table will be rolled multiple times.

Marks of War: 600

Yakamaru can only drop one item from this table. If no armour piece or Mazcab ability codex is dropped, the player will receive teci.

A player that owns all six pieces of achto legs and bodies may continue to receive achto armour as drops, but the drop order will no longer be enforced. For example, it is possible to receive a second Achto Teralith leggings, followed by a third Achto Teralith leggings.

Otherwise, armour is gained from Yakamaru in the following order: legs then body.

Progressing in the drop order requires collecting all three of the previous equipment slot's achto equipment, so in order to receive an Achto Primeval robe top, they would have to get all Achto Tempest, Primeval and Teralith legs. The Achto equipment gained from each equipment slot is based on the combat style the player dealt the most damage with during the kill they obtained that armour; if the equipment piece corresponding to the used style is not owned, that is always gotten before the others, and otherwise there are equal odds of obtaining armour corresponding to one of the unused styles.

When killed in the wilderness with achto armour, it will drop a specified amount of coins if you die.

drops.notes: The base chance to obtain any armour piece is 1/20, or 1/18 with maximum reputation. If all armour pieces are owned, this chance is multiplied by 1/6. Otherwise, the chosen armour piece is determined by the missing armour pieces (in order: legs then body) and the combat style used.

sections.description: Each kill of a sinkholes monster has a chance to drop a card. If a card has not yet been dropped for the player the chance is 1/3, else if the monster is combat level 85 or higher the chance is 1/4, otherwise the chance is 1/6. If a card is dropped, one of them is dropped from the distribution: 16% for each of locust, leech, and mantis; 10% for each of mosquito, yak, and bunyip; 8% for titan; 5% for meerkats; and 3% for each of ibis, phoenix, and smoke devil.
